question: In a certain code language, ‘CARDIO’ is written as ‘& * ^ % $ #”, ‘PARA’ is written as ‘$ % S %’ and ‘CAR’ is written as ‘# $ %*. Which of the following can be the code for ‘RADIO’ in that language?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15d4e688c8bdc2766cb74c67a7c0d12a85a1e60bc448f376b860b7949a5ae586.png] 

The logic followed here is:

‘CARDIO’ is written as ‘& * ^ % $ #”

‘PARA’ is written as ‘$ % S %’

 ‘CAR’ is written as ‘# $ %

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/889b4909e8dbc3e2012c527fff7adae7eb69df68d3f863bd40c41b70436c043a.png] 

So, the codes for R, A, D, I, and O will be:

R → $

A → %

D / I / O → & / * / ^

**‘RADIO’ is written as "% ^ * & $"**

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
